transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (NovaRetail CTO), Jorge Martinez (NovaRetail ML Eng), Lena Hofstad (Infra Lead), Tom Ellis (PM)

Summary (auto): Align on POC success criteria and acceptance tests; agree benchmark harness and timeline; assign action items.

[00:00] Alex Park: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya Rao: this is Priya, I'm CTO at NovaRetail, thanks.
[00:15] Jorge Martinez: Jorge here, ML eng, I'll run the dataset side.
[00:20] Lena Hofstad: Lena, infra.
[00:23] Tom Ellis: Tom, product.
[00:25] Samir Patel: Samir from Redwood, I'll cover benchmarks and the harness.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Maya, customer success - I'll coordinate scheduling.

[00:45] Alex Park: cool, so today's goal is to sign off success criteria for the POC, make sure we have clear go/no-go thresholds, and align on reporting format and timing. we have a draft doc in the drive, link in the calendar invite.
[01:10] Tom Ellis: yeah want to make sure we map this to product SLAs - primarily latency and relevance. our current baseline is the in-house hybrid model on EC2 g4dn that does about 120 qps at peak with p95 latency around 450 ms, and relevance score on our proprietary metric 'NR-F1' is 0.71.
[01:40] Priya Rao: and data residency is important, logs can't leave eu region for the pilot, we prefer the sandbox in eu-west-1.
[01:50] Alex Park: noted, we can spin up sandbox capacity in eu-west-1. Samir, can you enumerate the success criteria from Redwood's draft?
[02:05] Samir Patel: sure yep. the draft lists four core acceptance tests - throughput (sustained RPS for 30m), latency (p95 under threshold), quality (NR-F1 delta <= 0.03 versus baseline), and reliability/error rate (<0.5% token error or API exceptions). also cost per 1k tokens reference for reporting but not a hard gate.
[02:40] Jorge Martinez: on quality delta, how are you measuring NR-F1? is Redwood accepting our metric or do you need to re-run with your eval harness?
[02:52] Samir Patel: good q. we can ingest your NR-F1 labels and run the harness, or we can map to a proxy like ROUGE/bleu depending on the task. ideally we run your metric inside our eval harness so apples-to-apples. we'll need the labeled slice.
[03:10] Priya Rao: we'd prefer Redwood to run it since we want independent verification. we'll provide a labeled 2k-example slice with annotations. can you keep that private?
[03:25] Alex Park: absolutely, we'll store it in the project sandbox with restricted ACLs and destroy after the run unless you ask us to keep it. we can sign an annex if needed.

[03:45] Lena Hofstad: infra question - will you need VPC peering or can we use temporary secure upload? Also certs and SSO?
[03:55] Maya Chen: for the sandbox run we typically use a temporary S3 upload with a short-lived presigned URL and we can do VPC peering if desired for a private deployment test. which one do you prefer?
[04:10] Lena Hofstad: peering is better for security and to mirror our eventual private deployment, but we have to follow change window. can the run be scheduled in our next maintenance window on 2025-02-25?
[04:22] Samir Patel: we can do that week; we recommended week of 2025-02-24 earlier, sounds like the 25th aligns with your window.

[04:40] Alex Park: ok outlines - thresholds proposed: throughput sustained 200 rps for 30m (this is an example, Jorge you said 120 qps baseline, we're proposing 200 to show headroom), p95 latency <= 400 ms at 1k token avg, NR-F1 delta <= 0.03, error rate < 0.5%. Are these reasonable?
[05:05] Jorge Martinez: 200 feels ambitious vs our baseline; our traffic pattern is spiky though and we care about p95 more than sustained. could we scope two profiles: steady baseline 120 rps and burst 240 rps for 2 minutes?
[05:22] Alex Park: yes we can run multiple profiles. we'll capture both. acceptance needs both: p95 under threshold for baseline profile, and graceful degradation for burst profile (no more than 20% increase in p95).
[05:35] Tom Ellis: on reporting - we need a dashboard with per-route p50/p95/p99, token counts, cost estimate, and the evaluation summary with NR-F1 comparisons and example failure cases. CSV export would be helpful.
[05:50] Samir Patel: our standard runbook includes a Grafana dashboard and a downloadable CSV with per-request metrics and an eval report linking to flagged examples. we'll share a template before the run.

[06:10] Priya Rao: SLA-ish question - for the POC if the model returns hallucinations at a higher rate than baseline, what's the remediation? do you support rollbacks to a smaller model?
[06:22] Alex Park: yes we have model variants; the idea is to test the primary candidate and also have a fallback model pinned that we can route to if quality drops. for the POC we'll capture regression and we can propose mitigations like prompt tuning, temperature constraints, or fallback routing. but the pass/fail is defined by the NR-F1 delta.

[06:40] Jorge Martinez: one more - tokenization differences can affect the cost and metrics, do you normalize tokens vs our baseline?
[06:48] Samir Patel: we report raw token counts by tokenizer used and we can normalize to your tokenizer as well; helpful to provide your exact tokenizer version.

[07:00] Alex Park: timeline recap - today sign-off on thresholds, Alex to send final doc by 2/20; Samir to share harness and runbook by 2/21; customer to confirm dataset slice by 2/21; schedule run for 2/25 in maintenance window; run results and deck back within 3 business days after run. sound good?
[07:20] Priya Rao: yes. quick note on compliance - we need audit logs and retention settings to be documented.
[07:28] Maya Chen: will include audit log retention, KMS usage details and data deletion process in the security annex.

[07:45] Tom Ellis: about reporting format - can you include per-test pass/fail matrix and a slide with recommended knobs to reach production SLAs?
[07:55] Samir Patel: yes we'll include a remediation slide and configuration recommendations (batching, kv cache, quantization profile).

[08:10] Priya Rao: pricing - rough estimate for the Dedicated-like config for this workload? we need to budget.
[08:18] Alex Park: we won't have final pricing until we size a dedicated cluster but we'll include a cost projection for the benchmark run and an estimate for a dedicated 4-GPU pool. not a formal quote, just a planning number.

[08:35] Jorge Martinez: can we test both hosted variant (Redwood hosted) and a simulated dedicated config? to see differences in latency and cost.
[08:42] Samir Patel: yes we can do two runs: hosted and dedicated-simulated (same runtime but pinned resources). we'll capture both.

[09:00] Alex Park: ok recording a few acceptance test details verbatim so the doc is exact:
- Test A (Baseline throughput): 30m sustained at 120 rps, p95 < 450 ms, NR-F1 delta <= 0.03, error rate < 0.5%
- Test B (Burst): 2 minute bursts at 240 rps, p95 increase <= 20% vs baseline, no more than 1% timed-out requests
- Test C (Quality): full labeled slice evaluation, NR-F1 compared to NovaRetail baseline, pass if delta <= 0.03 and no systemic failure modes (e.g., hallucination spike > 5%)
- Test D (Stability): 24-hour smoke test for error patterns (optional for POC, recommended for dedup)

[09:50] Priya Rao: those look good. one clarifying question: what is the definition of 'hallucination spike' you used?
[09:58] Samir Patel: we define hallucination as false-entity insertion relative to labels; a spike is >5% of examples showing that behavior. we'll include examples flagged in the report.

[10:20] Lena Hofstad: for the peering, I'll need an IP allowlist and cookbook for the Terraform module to create the peering. I can sign an IP SLA for the sandbox if you provide the details.
[10:30] Samir Patel: we'll share the peering terraform and ip ranges; expect to get that to you by 2/21.

[11:00] Alex Park: any other blockers?
[11:05] Jorge Martinez: dataset anonymization - can't share PII. we'll strip PII but keep labels. is that ok?
[11:12] Maya Chen: yes that's common; please share the anonymization script or steps so we can verify.

[11:30] Tom Ellis: timeline again: final doc by 2/20, harness/runbook by 2/21, dataset by 2/21, run 2/25, deliver results by 2/28.
[11:45] Alex Park: agreed. I'll send a calendar hold for the run and include the doc link.

[11:55] Priya Rao: thanks everyone. looking forward to the run.
[12:00] Alex Park: thanks, we will follow up with the artifacts, meeting adjourned.

Auto-generated action items (end): Alex to share doc, Samir to share harness/runbook, Jorge to provide dataset slice, Lena to provision peering details.
